target.title: fix(imessage): prevent duplicate messages after delayed sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an iMessage send could complete through `imsg`'s AppleScript fallback after a private-bridge stall, while OpenClaw reported a timeout to the calling agent. The agent then retried the apparently failed send, producing duplicate messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated send timeout is increased from 150 seconds to 180 seconds. This lets the outer RPC outlive `imsg`'s 150-second bridge deadline plus its fallback verification window, while leaving the 10-second probe timeout unchanged.

This is intentionally a boundary fix rather than a second delivery-verification implementation in OpenClaw. In the observed incident, the delivered rows stored their text in `attributedBody`, so OpenClaw's plain `message.text` recovery path could not reliably identify them. `imsg` already owns that verification.

## User Impact

Users should receive one message instead of duplicates when the private iMessage bridge stalls but the fallback send succeeds.

## Evidence

### Redacted live failure timeline before the fix

One cron session issued three sends of the same text to the same chat:

```text
09:00:33  send request 1 started
09:03:14  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7080 persisted
09:03:19  calling agent retried
09:05:57  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7081 persisted
09:06:19  calling agent used direct imsg send; outgoing row 7082 persisted
```

Recipient and message text are omitted. The matching timeout and persistence timestamps show that the first two sends completed at the point the 150-second outer timer rejected them.

### Dependency and caller contract

- `imsg` assigns send actions a [150-second bridge deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeProtocol.swift#L28-L39), which its [bridge client enforces](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeClient.swift#L97-L121).
- Auto transport [falls through to AppleScript after a bridge error and then verifies the persisted send](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/RPCServer%2BHandlers.swift#L271-L320).
- The persisted-message verifier [polls for up to 8 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/SentMessageVerifier.swift#L13-L26).
- OpenClaw selects the dedicated default in [`sendMessageIMessage`](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L720-L725) and [passes it to the single RPC request](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L871-L885). OpenClaw does not retry this request internally; the calling agent retried after receiving the ambiguous timeout.

### Deterministic delayed-boundary proof

The focused regression test models `imsg` returning successfully at 158 seconds, after the old outer deadline but within the new one. It asserts that the send resolves with the fallback message GUID and that OpenClaw makes exactly one RPC request.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`

### Live patched-build proof

The branch was rebased onto current `main`, built, and run through Lobster's exclusive iMessage dev-gateway proof workflow. A temporary copy of the morning context-question cron was triggered once with an explicit private destination:

```text
status:          ok
duration:        5207 ms
deliveryStatus:  delivered
database rows:   1
row:             7086 at 10:58:38 local time
```

The recipient, message text, and GUID are omitted. The unique output persisted as exactly one outgoing row. This live run completed through the normal fast bridge path; the 158-second fallback boundary is covered deterministically above because forcing a real bridge stall would require restarting Messages with a stale readiness marker and would introduce an avoidable delivery race.

After proof, the temporary dev cron was removed, the dev gateway stopped, and production was restored healthy on port 18789 with exactly one `imsg rpc` process.

Additional validation:

- Full branch build passed on current `main`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final Codex branch autoreview: no findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, implementation, test updates, and independent review were performed with Codex under maintainer supervision.

target.title: fix(openai-http): keep SSE argument chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Replace `String.prototype.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` in `splitArgumentsForStreaming` to prevent SSE argument chunks from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. The old code could produce invalid JSON when multi-byte characters (e.g., CJK, emoji) straddled the 256-char chunk boundary, causing downstream parse failures on the client.

Fixes #110642

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: SSE streaming chunks of tool_call arguments can contain truncated/invalid UTF-16 when the 256-char boundary falls inside a surrogate pair, causing the client to receive malformed JSON.

**Root Cause**: `splitArgumentsForStreaming()` in `src/gateway/openai-http.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units without awareness of surrogate pairs. When a multi-byte character spans positions 255-256, the slice produces a broken chunk.

**Solution**: Import and use `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, which ensures surrogate pairs are never split. The loop increment is changed from a fixed `+= chunkSize` to `+= chunk.length` (with `|| 1` fallback) because the safe slice may return 256 or 257 characters.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: SSE chunking of tool_call arguments to not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs

target.title: fix(cron): honor explicit announce delivery on system-event jobs
target.body:
## Problem

A cron job created with `payload.kind="systemEvent"` and no explicit `sessionTarget` defaults to `sessionTarget="main"` (see `normalizeCronJobInput`). Main-session jobs enqueue their text into the owning session and never take `assertDeliverySupport`'s announce path. So when a caller *also* attaches an explicit delivery block:

```jsonc
{
  "schedule": { "kind": "every", "everyMs": 86400000 },
  "payload":  { "kind": "systemEvent", "text": "Check the incident dashboard" },
  "delivery": { "mode": "announce", "channel": "telegram", "to": "..." }
}
```

...the entire `cron.add` is rejected:

```
cron channel delivery config is only supported for sessionTarget="isolated"
```

This is a very natural shape for "watch X and notify me" scheduled jobs: emit a systemEvent reminder plus an announce delivery block. Instead of delivering, the request **fails closed** — the job is never created at all. The caller expressed clear intent (announce to a channel) and got a hard error.

## Fix

When a system-event job **explicitly requests announce delivery** but does **not** pin a session target, isolate it and carry the event text over as an agent turn, so the requested delivery is honored via the existing isolated-agent announce path.

Scope is deliberately narrow:
- Only triggers when `delivery` normalizes to an announce request (`mode: "announce"`, or a concrete channel/to with mode omitted — matching how `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` already interprets it).
- System-event jobs that **don't** request channel delivery still default to `sessionTarget="main"`, unchanged.
- An explicit `sessionTarget="main"` set by the caller is untouched (this block only runs when `sessionTarget` is absent).
- Empty/blank systemEvent text falls back to the previous `main` default rather than creating an empty agent turn.

## Tests

`src/cron/normalize.test.ts`:
- isolates a system-event job that requests announce delivery (asserts `sessionTarget="isolated"`, payload converted to `agentTurn`, delivery preserved)
- keeps a plain system-event job on `main` when no delivery is requested

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveInitialCronDelivery` in `src/cron/service/initial-delivery.ts` only checks `sessionTarget === "isolated"` when deciding whether to inject default `{ mode: "announce" }` delivery. All other cron code paths already treat `"isolated"`, `"current"`, and `"session:"` as equivalent for this purpose, creating an inconsistency.

## Why This Change Was Made

After #98947 restored persistent session targets, the three sessionTarget values are treated identically in:

target.title: feat(clients): adopt model controls, session management, and keyboard history recall on iOS
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS/web chat parity rounds (#110254, #110276, #110339, #110347) landed all capability in shared `OpenClawKit`, but iOS still only forwarded transport fields: no model controls, no session groups/batch/inspector, no worktree-aware creation, and no hardware-keyboard input history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt the shared surfaces on iOS with iOS-idiomatic UX, keeping the shared API additive:

- **Model controls** (`ChatModelControlsMenu.swift`, wired from ChatPro's existing action menu): provider-grouped model picker via the shared `ChatModelPickerStore` (pinned + recents first, default badges), thinking with `Default (inherited)`, Fast as Default/On/Off (Default patches `fastMode: null`; display rides `effectiveFastMode`; legacy `auto` not re-selectable), verbosity as Default/off/on/full (Default patches null).
- **Session management**: the sessions affordance now presents the shared `ChatSessionsSheet` (groups, select/batch mode, inspector); advanced new-session options (agent, managed worktree, base ref) present in a medium-detent sheet.
- **Transport** (`IOSGatewayChatTransport.swift`): exact-route leases for settings, mutations, groups, and new-session; 6-arg `createSession` mapping `agentId`/`worktree`/`worktreeBaseRef`; settings patches forward the fast-mode double-optional including explicit null. Implementing the real overload removes iOS from the fail-closed protocol default.
- **Input history**: hardware-keyboard ↑ starts recall only from an empty draft; active recall supports ↑/↓; non-empty and soft-wrapped drafts keep native caret movement; no touch-UX change (shared `ChatInputHistory` state machine).

## User Impact

iOS chat users get the same model, Fast, verbosity, and thinking controls as web/macOS, full session organization (groups, batch actions, inspector, worktree sessions from a chosen base ref), and terminal-style input history on hardware keyboards.

## Evidence

- Shared OpenClawKit suite: 994 tests green (48 XCTest + 946 Swift Testing, 81+ suites).
- iOS `build-for-testing` (generic simulator, Xcode project via xcodegen): green — app and test targets compile.
- `IOSGatewayChatTransportTests`: 15/15, including advanced-create encoding, fast-mode set/null, and groups-lease methods/params/decoding.
- `pnpm format:swift` clean; `pnpm lint:swift` 0 violations; all touched files under the 1500-line cap; `git diff --check` clean.

target.title: fix(acp): reject malformed session list cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACP clients and bundled Pi/OpenCode session catalog callers could send a malformed opaque pagination cursor and receive a plausible session or transcript page instead of an invalid-cursor error.

Node's base64url decoder ignores some invalid characters and accepts non-canonical padding. The ACP and plugin input paths also trimmed cursor strings before decoding. Because the original token was not checked exactly, values that OpenClaw never emitted could still reach Gateway, Pi session-store, or OpenCode CLI pagination.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each owning path now preserves the original opaque cursor and verifies that decoded bytes round-trip to the exact unpadded base64url token before parsing JSON or using the offset. This follows the existing strict encoded-request pattern in OpenClaw while keeping ACP and plugin ownership separate.

Valid cursors and the encoded cursor format are unchanged. This does not change schemas, limits, storage, or the Anthropic catalog path; the latter has separate open cursor-validation work in #104967.

## User Impact

Malformed ACP, Pi, and OpenCode catalog cursors now fail clearly instead of silently returning misleading pagination results. Cursors returned by OpenClaw continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Malformed session pagination cursors containing ignored characters, non-canonical padding, or surrounding whitespace were accepted as valid.

**Environment tested:** Linux, Node 24.15.0, pinned OpenClaw main reproduction plus the patched local Gateway, real WebSocket transport, real `openclaw acp` subprocess, and ACP stdio JSON-RPC frames.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Started the patched Gateway, spawned `node openclaw.mjs acp --url ws://127.0.0.1:<port> --token-file <file>`, sent ACP `initialize`, then sent `session/list` with no cursor, a canonical cursor, the same cursor with an appended `$`, and the canonical cursor wrapped in spaces.

target.title: fix(ssh-verify): preserve active cooldown entries during prune
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The cooldown prune function's size-bound enforcement loop (`while` loop in `pruneCooldowns`) evicts the oldest entry without checking whether it is still active (unexpired). This means a cooldown entry that is still in effect — where `expiry > nowMs` — could be evicted just because the cache is over `MAX_COOLDOWN_ENTRIES`, causing the system to re-probe a recently failed host before its cooldown period has elapsed.

**Root Cause**: The `while` loop that enforces the hard size bound (`MAX_COOLDOWN_ENTRIES = 512`) on `cooldownExpiryByKey` unconditionally deletes the oldest entry when the map exceeds the limit. Unlike the `for` loop above it (which only removes expired entries), the `while` loop has no guard to distinguish expired entries (safe to evict) from active ones (must be preserved).

**Solution**: Before evicting the oldest entry in the size-bound enforcement loop, read its expiry and check whether it is still active (`expiry > nowMs`). If it is, break out of the loop — the cache is over-full only with active entries, which should not be evicted. The `for` loop above already handles cleanup of expired entries.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: CI test suite (unit tests for `node-pairing-ssh-verify` module)

**Exact steps run after this patch**:
```
npx vitest run src/gateway/node-pairing-ssh-verify.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  57 passed (57)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 57 tests pass across 3 test files. The `pruneCooldowns` function now correctly preserves active cooldown entries when enforcing the size bound.

**What was not tested**: Integration/e2e test with a real SSH connection. The fix is in process-local bookkeeping logic covered by existing unit tests.

## Tests and validation

- `pruneCooldowns` unit tests cover the size-bound enforcement path
- The fix adds a guard: `if (expiry > nowMs) break;` — preserving active entries
- No behavioral change for the expired-entry cleanup path (the `for` loop above)

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#110660 shipped per-bubble rewind and fork-from-message in the web Control UI, backed by `sessions.rewind`/`sessions.fork`. The native SwiftUI chat shared by the macOS and iOS apps had no equivalent — its bubbles had no transcript actions at all, and the typed protocol models for the two RPCs were never registered for Swift/Kotlin generation. Follow-up agreed in #110660.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Registers `SessionsRewindParams/Result` and `SessionsForkParams/Result` in `ProtocolSchemas` (they existed in the TypeBox schema but were missed for codegen) and regenerates the Swift models; Kotlin outputs were already current. Generation ran twice with identical output. No protocol version bump.
- `OpenClawChatUI` message context menus (all three row variants) gain **Rewind to Here** and **Fork from Here** for user messages with a persisted transcript id (`__openclaw.id` via `transcriptMessageID`), disabled while the agent is working (`hasBlockingRunActivity`/`isSending`/`isAborting` — the same gate as compact).
- Rewind: calls the RPC, clears reply/provisional state, seeds the composer with the returned text, and refreshes history; a `sessionsChanged reason:"rewind"` event from another client now also refreshes the open session. Fork: staleness-guarded switch to the returned session key, composer seeded there; on any post-RPC staleness it falls back to a session-list refresh instead of navigating.
- Transport: two new `OpenClawChatTransport` methods with default-throwing impls, named distinctly from the existing whole-session `forkSession(parentKey:)`; macOS implementation extracts a shared server-lease-guarded dispatch helper (net dedup), iOS routes through the ordered `requestSessionMutation` path. Dispatch intentionally mirrors the shipped `forkSession(key:)` shape (per-request server-lease guard + staleness re-checks) rather than the patch-flow route lease, which doesn't expose fork/rewind — documented inline.

## User Impact

macOS and iOS chat bubbles now offer the same rewind and fork-from-message actions as the web UI: long-press/right-click a user message to rewind the session to just before it (text returns to the composer) or branch a new session from that point. Gateway-side gating (busy runs, external-harness sessions) applies identically.

## Evidence

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --parallel` — 988 tests, 84 suites, all passing (19 new: request builders, rewind refresh + composer seed, fork switch + staleness, busy gating, remote-event refresh; plus macOS transport mapping tests).
- Protocol generators run twice with byte-identical generated output; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/native-protocol-levels.guard.test.ts` green.
- SwiftFormat/oxfmt/oxlint clean; `git diff --check` clean.
- Autoreview (codex `gpt-5.6-sol`): one finding proposing the patch-flow route lease for fork-then-switch — rejected after verification: the shipped `forkSession(key:)` sibling uses the same lease-free dispatch, the lease API doesn't expose fork/rewind, and this flow adds a session-list refresh fallback the sibling lacks; the contract is documented inline.
- Known local-only issue: `swift test --package-path apps/macos` fails to build the test target on baseline `GatewayProcessManagerTests.swift` (Sendable strictness, file untouched by this PR, last modified on main weeks ago) — the feature sources compile; CI's macos-swift lane is authoritative.

target.title: fix(qa): repair WhatsApp live scenario regressions
target.body:
AI-assisted: Codex.

## Summary

Fixes regressions in the live WhatsApp QA harness that prevented parts of the scenario fleet from exercising the selected test account correctly.

- Generic declarative flows now perform their own configuration instead of being rejected for not having a code-defined WhatsApp scenario ID.
- Account-specific configuration and destructive array replacement paths use the account selected by `--sut-account`.
- The linked QA driver is added to `commands.ownerAllowFrom` while preserving existing owners.
- The group access-control fixture uses the configured WhatsApp QA identity for mention gating.
- WhatsApp QA target formatting remains inside the WhatsApp QA adapter instead of loading another channel runtime.

This PR changes QA code and scenario fixtures only. It does not change the WhatsApp production runtime.

## Account selection

The shared live-transport CLI already defines the account contract:

- `--sut-account foo` configures and tests `channels.whatsapp.accounts.foo`.
- Omitting the option uses the shared default account ID, `sut`.

Scenarios now follow the adapter's selected account. They do not search for accounts or fall back between account names.

## Cause

The affected scenarios were migrated from a code-driven runner to declarative YAML flows. The previous runner consistently carried the selected account ID into generated configuration. The migrated pairing flow instead authorized replacement of a fixed `accounts.sut.allowFrom` path, while generic declarative flows could be rejected before their own setup ran. The default `sut` account masked the account-path mismatch until the fleet ran with another valid account ID.

## Validation

- Local live WhatsApp fleet: 52 scenarios discovered, 52 passed, 0 missing, 0 failed.
- Focused WhatsApp QA runtime and scenario tests passed.
- Scenario 1, `whatsapp-access-control-dm-disabled`, passed through the generic declarative-flow path.
- QA-only scope: 7 files changed; no `extensions/whatsapp/src/**` files.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep channel lifecycle outside released request admission
target.body:
Closes #110697

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel accounts started or restarted from a short-lived gateway request could stop accepting later work after that request finished. Provider callbacks, approval bootstrap follow-up, and automatic restarts could retain the released request's admission context and fail with `GatewayDrainingError` even though the process-global gateway fence was still open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel lifecycle work is process-lifetime, not request-lifetime. The channel manager now creates approval-bootstrap work and the full provider -> cleanup -> auto-restart promise chain outside the current gateway request admission root, using the existing `runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission` helper. Process-global restart and suspension fences remain authoritative; this change only stops a released request root from poisoning long-lived channel tasks.

Compatibility: no config, protocol, or public API change; callers of `createChannelManager` / `startChannel` keep the same surface. Performance: one ALS exit at lifecycle creation, no request-time discovery. Usability: channels stay responsive after the starting RPC/reload ends. Security: does not reopen admission during real drain or suspension.

## User Impact

Long-running channel accounts remain able to accept work after the gateway request or reload that started them has completed. Real process restart and suspension still refuse new work normally.

## Evidence

Exact current head: `a73e8d29d7fbe8e245c0e37f386dc14de8f32b2d`.

- [Full CI run 29649706201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29649706201): passed on prior head, including all four QA Smoke CI profiles.
- Focused production-patch proof on `ca8722dbbc`: `src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` 53/53 passed; `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` 17/17 passed.
- Formatting/lint on the touched production and test files: `oxfmt --check` passed; `oxlint` reported 0 warnings and 0 errors; `git diff --check` clean.
- Isolated QA scenario: `qa/scenarios/channels/channel-lifecycle-admission.yaml`.

New focused cases:

1. `does not inherit a released request admission into a channel task`
2. `does not inherit a released request admission into approval bootstrap work`
3. `does not inherit a released request admission into an automatic channel restart`

## Real behavior proof

Isolated real gateway + `qa-channel` + `mock-openai` run at head `a73e8d29d7` (after the scenario harness fix that drives suspend prepare/resume over Admin HTTP, matching docs for hosts that cannot keep a WebSocket open across suspension).

Command:

```bash
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm openclaw qa suite \
  --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --scenario channel-lifecycle-admission \
  --channel-driver qa-channel \
  --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/channel-lifecycle-admission-proof3
```

Result: **passed=1 failed=0** in ~11s.

Redacted step transcript:

```text
[qa-suite] scenario pass (1/1): channel-lifecycle-admission
[qa-suite] run complete: passed=1 failed=0 skipped=0 total=1

Step 1: accepts channel work after the starting RPC root is released — pass
{
  "stopped": { "channel": "qa-channel", "accountId": "default", "stopped": true },
  "started": { "channel": "qa-channel", "accountId": "default", "started": true },
  "firstOutbound": "QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RPC-OK"
}

Step 2: preserves process-global suspension refusal and resumes delivery — pass
{
  "suspension": {
    "status": "ready",
    "suspensionId": "424d4adc-…-ce424fc01836",
    "activeCount": 0,
    "blockers": []
  },
  "suspendedCallError": "channels.status unavailable during gateway suspension (reason=gateway-suspending, phase=prepared)",
  "resumed": { "ok": true, "status": "running", "resumed": true },
  "resumedOutbound": "QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RESUME-OK"
}
```

Observable sequence matched the review acceptance criteria:

1. `channels.stop` / `channels.start` return for the real QA channel account.
2. After the start RPC root is gone, inbound work produces `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RPC-OK`.
3. Prepared suspension rejects ordinary `channels.status` with `UNAVAILABLE` / `gateway-suspending`.
4. `gateway.suspend.resume` returns `running`; inbound work then produces `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RESUME-OK`.

Scenario note: suite `gateway.call` opens a new WebSocket per RPC, and a prepared suspension rejects new handshakes by design (`docs/gateway/external-apps.md`). The scenario therefore enables the bundled `admin-http-rpc` plugin for prepare / refuse / resume control while still exercising the real channel delivery path on qa-channel.

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok and Codex).

## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

target.title: Add experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the canonical Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report incomplete installs, missing or modified agents, workspace drift, package drift/incomplete state, MCP ownership drift, unresolved cron ownership, and orphaned subordinate rows
- corroborate cron ownership against every page of one stable live Gateway inventory snapshot
- preserve source MCP placeholders while inspecting runtime config so resolved credentials cannot create false drift
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution absent unless `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`

## Contract

- doctor reuses `claws status` ownership states instead of independently interpreting managed resources
- absent and pre-Claws state produce no Claw findings and no Claw-created state directory, database, schema, migration, chmod, checkpoint, or journal-mode change
- existing state is observed through one read-only handle; WAL-backed state remains visible, while missing experimental ownership tables are treated as empty only in read-only mode
- unreadable, invalid, or forward-version state databases return one structured error finding rather than aborting doctor
- source MCP config is read through the canonical source-config API; `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders remain unexpanded
- live cron health requires matching scheduler job id, declaration key, owner, enabled state, and execution-relevant digest; Gateway failure or a changing inventory reports `unknown`, never healthy
- the Claw collector is advisory and does not mutate config, files, scheduler state, provenance, database bytes, metadata, schema, or journal mode; OpenClaw's existing config-observation behavior outside this collector is unchanged

## Verification

- current-head GitHub CI is green, including `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, lint, max-lines ratchet, compact shards, and `openclaw/ci-gate`
- 317 affected tests passed in WSL across shared state, Doctor, health contributions, lifecycle state, workspace, provenance, MCP, cron, and CLI
- focused Oxlint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and Kysely guardrails pass
- absent/pre-Claws tests prove the collector creates no state and changes no bytes
- existing-state coverage compares database bytes, mtime, mode, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`, and `journal_mode`; WAL regression coverage proves uncheckpointed migrations remain visible
- invalid and newer-schema tests prove open failures become structured findings and handles close cleanly

## Real behavior proof

Exact head `ec41651ee29aa40573420ef00b038c56d155a797`, Node 24.15.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 WSL2.

1. Created the package-free `workspace-agent` fixture through real `claws add --dry-run --json`, followed by consented `claws add --yes --plan-integrity ... --json`.
2. Pointed the read-only Doctor invocation at an absent source config to produce a real missing-agent finding without exercising OpenClaw's separate config-observation writer.
3. Held a concurrent SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` writer open with `openclaw.sqlite-wal` and `openclaw.sqlite-shm` present.
4. Hashed every state entry's type, relative path, size, mode, mtime, symlink target, and file contents before and after the gated check.

```text
OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS unset:
{"ok":false,"checksRun":0,"checksSkipped":52,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/lint-selection","severity":"error","message":"Unknown health check id selected by --only: core/doctor/claws-state.","path":"core/doctor/claws-state"}]}

OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1:
STATE_SIDECARS=present
CONCURRENT_WRITER=held-immediate-transaction
BEFORE=7d7542203b05c921f70b7f7bcc88849d744ca053586236c09bdf534977b4c448
AFTER=7d7542203b05c921f70b7f7bcc88849d744ca053586236c09bdf534977b4c448
UNCHANGED=yes
{"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":52,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/claws-state","severity":"warning","message":"Claw-owned agent \"workspace-agent\" is missing from config.","source":"doctor","path":"agents.list.workspace-agent","target":"workspace-agent","requirement":"Claw-owned agent config should match its recorded install digest","fixHint":"Inspect the agent change before removing or replacing Claw-owned state."}]}
```

The exit code is `1` because the intentionally induced warning is reported. Private paths are redacted.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102406 MCP ownership
- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics
- Next: #102959 uses the same ownership model for grouped update planning

Doctor lands after every add/remove owner so it can reuse one authoritative status model instead of inventing partial resource checks. The Claws CLI and doctor surface remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound ci-run-timings git and GitHub CLI operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a git network operation (`git ls-remote`) in the ci-run-timings script could hang indefinitely when the Git remote is unreachable. Without a timeout, the script would block on network I/O until the job timeout, stalling CI timing reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", "origin", "main"], ??` call performs a network operation to list remote refs. All network-touching `execFileSync` calls must include a timeout and kill signal. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109325 (docker attestation) and #109982 (npm resume GitHub lookups).

## User Impact

CI timing reports can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely when the Git remote is unresponsive.

## Evidence

- The change adds a `CI_RUN_TIMINGS_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", ??)` call site.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/ci-run-timings.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/verify-docker-attestations.mjs` (#109325) and `scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` (#109968).

## What Problem This Solves The `show_widget` tool description rides in every agent context on every turn, so its token cost is paid constantly. target.title: feat(ui): approval UX overhaul — inline cards, fair queue, shortcuts, badges
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Pending exec/plugin approvals are easy to miss and slow to act on: the global modal shows only the newest request (starving older ones toward their 30-minute expiry), there is no in-conversation approval surface, no per-agent/per-session indicators, no expiry visibility, and no keyboard path.

## Why This Change Was Made
Fleet operators supervising multiple agents need approvals to be scannable and fast to decide without losing safety. Queue becomes oldest-first with a selectable list; the active chat session renders its approval inline between transcript and composer (suppressed from the modal); Ctrl/Cmd chord shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter allow once, +Shift always, +D deny) with auto-repeat guards; live mm:ss expiry countdown; per-agent count pills and per-session warning badges in the sidebar. Errors are scoped per approval id so one request's failure never hides another's. The displayed card is pinned so late-arriving requests cannot swap the command under the user's cursor.

## User Impact
Approvals surface where the user is working, oldest requests stop starving, fleet state is visible per agent/session, and keyboard users get a safe fast path. No gateway or protocol changes; UI-only.

target.title: feat(android): platform trust for public gateway certs + manual fingerprint pinning
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app pins a TLS fingerprint for every gateway, including hosts with publicly valid certificates. For a Tailscale Funnel gateway on `*.ts.net` with a Let's Encrypt cert, that means a "fingerprint changed" re-verification prompt every 60–90 day renewal — recurring friction that trains users to click through security prompts. Separately, when the TLS probe failed with no stored pin, connecting hard-failed with no escape hatch, and a malformed stored pin silently degraded instead of failing closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Platform trust for public certs.** Before prompting, the probe performs a real handshake against the system CA store with `endpointIdentificationAlgorithm="HTTPS"` and SNI. If the chain validates and the hostname matches, the connection uses platform trust — no pin stored, no prompt, renewals just work. A conservative candidate classifier (rejects `.local`, IPv4/IPv6 literals, single-label and malformed hostnames) keeps LAN endpoints on the existing pin flow.
- **Existing pins stay authoritative.** A valid public chain never silently clears a user-accepted pin. On mismatch with a system-trusted cert, the changed-pin prompt gains an explicit "Use system trust" choice; picking it clears the pin once, after which renewals are automatic. Replacing a pin always requires explicit confirmation.
- **Discovery cannot become identity.** Saved discovered endpoints still require a stored fingerprint for reconnect eligibility — mDNS advertisements are attacker-controllable on the LAN, and a DNS-shaped advertised host with the attacker's own valid cert must not inherit a saved gateway's credentials.
- **Out-of-band manual pinning.** When the probe can't capture a certificate, the trust dialog accepts a pasted SHA-256 fingerprint obtained on the gateway host (tolerates `sha256:` prefixes, colons, whitespace, case; requires 64 hex), then enforces it on connect — stronger verification than eyeball-TOFU, and an escape hatch where there was a dead end.
- Hardening along the way: malformed stored pins now fail closed at handshake time; both probe attempts share one connect+handshake budget so a TCP-accepting, TLS-stalling host cannot double probe latency; the trust decision is a closed sealed type (`SystemTrusted` / `PinnedTrust` / `PromptRequired` / `Failed`).

## User Impact

Funnel/public-cert gateways connect without fingerprint ceremony and stop re-prompting on cert renewals. LAN and IP gateways keep trust-on-first-use pinning with the existing first-seen and changed-pin dialogs. Users who deliberately pinned a public host keep their pin unless they explicitly switch. Two new user-facing strings, translated across all 21 locales.

## Evidence

- `GatewayTlsTest` (trust-decision matrix incl. supersession rows, candidate classifier, fingerprint normalizer, probe-budget splitting), `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest`, `GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest`: green on both Play and ThirdParty flavors (14 + 51 + 2 per flavor).
- `:app:ktlintCheck`, `android-app-i18n` check, `git diff --check`: green.
- Structured autoreview: three rounds; four accepted findings fixed (two P1s — discovery-eligibility identity binding, silent pin supersession — plus fail-closed pin handling and probe-latency amplification); final round clean: "consistently adds Android platform trust for eligible DNS gateways while preserving existing certificate pins."
- All `resolveTlsParams` call sites verified `allowTOFU=false`, so the system-trust path connects with platform trust and real hostname verification (no TOFU fallback).

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep channel lifecycle outside released request admission
target.body:
Closes #110697

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel accounts started or restarted from a short-lived gateway request could stop accepting later work after that request finished. Provider callbacks, approval bootstrap follow-up, and automatic restarts could retain the released request's admission context and fail with `GatewayDrainingError` even though the process-global gateway fence was still open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel lifecycle work is process-lifetime, not request-lifetime. The channel manager now creates approval-bootstrap work and the full provider -> cleanup -> auto-restart promise chain outside the current gateway request admission root, using the existing `runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission` helper. Process-global restart and suspension fences remain authoritative; this change only stops a released request root from poisoning long-lived channel tasks.

Compatibility: no config, protocol, or public API change; callers of `createChannelManager` / `startChannel` keep the same surface. Performance: one ALS exit at lifecycle creation, no request-time discovery. Usability: channels stay responsive after the starting RPC/reload ends. Security: does not reopen admission during real drain or suspension.

## User Impact

Long-running channel accounts remain able to accept work after the gateway request or reload that started them has completed. Real process restart and suspension still refuse new work normally.

## Evidence

Exact current head: `a73e8d29d7fbe8e245c0e37f386dc14de8f32b2d`.

- [Full CI run 29649706201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29649706201): passed on prior head, including all four QA Smoke CI profiles.
- Focused production-patch proof on `ca8722dbbc`: `src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` 53/53 passed; `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` 17/17 passed.
- Formatting/lint on the touched production and test files: `oxfmt --check` passed; `oxlint` reported 0 warnings and 0 errors; `git diff --check` clean.
- Isolated QA scenario: `qa/scenarios/channels/channel-lifecycle-admission.yaml`.

New focused cases:

1. `does not inherit a released request admission into a channel task`
2. `does not inherit a released request admission into approval bootstrap work`
3. `does not inherit a released request admission into an automatic channel restart`

## Real behavior proof

Isolated real gateway + `qa-channel` + `mock-openai` run at head `a73e8d29d7` (after the scenario harness fix that drives suspend prepare/resume over Admin HTTP, matching docs for hosts that cannot keep a WebSocket open across suspension).

Command:

```bash
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm openclaw qa suite \
  --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --scenario channel-lifecycle-admission \
  --channel-driver qa-channel \
  --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/channel-lifecycle-admission-proof3
```

Result: **passed=1 failed=0** in ~11s.

Redacted step transcript:

```text
[qa-suite] scenario pass (1/1): channel-lifecycle-admission
[qa-suite] run complete: passed=1 failed=0 skipped=0 total=1

Step 1: accepts channel work after the starting RPC root is released — pass
{
  "stopped": { "channel": "qa-channel", "accountId": "default", "stopped": true },
  "started": { "channel": "qa-channel", "accountId": "default", "started": true },
  "firstOutbound": "QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RPC-OK"
}

Step 2: preserves process-global suspension refusal and resumes delivery — pass
{
  "suspension": {
    "status": "ready",
    "suspensionId": "424d4adc-…-ce424fc01836",
    "activeCount": 0,
    "blockers": []
  },
  "suspendedCallError": "channels.status unavailable during gateway suspension (reason=gateway-suspending, phase=prepared)",
  "resumed": { "ok": true, "status": "running", "resumed": true },
  "resumedOutbound": "QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RESUME-OK"
}
```

Observable sequence matched the review acceptance criteria:

1. `channels.stop` / `channels.start` return for the real QA channel account.
2. After the start RPC root is gone, inbound work produces `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RPC-OK`.
3. Prepared suspension rejects ordinary `channels.status` with `UNAVAILABLE` / `gateway-suspending`.
4. `gateway.suspend.resume` returns `running`; inbound work then produces `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RESUME-OK`.

Scenario note: suite `gateway.call` opens a new WebSocket per RPC, and a prepared suspension rejects new handshakes by design (`docs/gateway/external-apps.md`). The scenario therefore enables the bundled `admin-http-rpc` plugin for prepare / refuse / resume control while still exercising the real channel delivery path on qa-channel.

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: fix(gateway): isolate wizard exits from shared process
target.body:
Closes #110545

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway RPC wizard sessions inherited two CLI-owned behaviors that do not belong to a shared host process:

- setup/channel runners could terminate the Gateway through `runtime.exit()`;
- remote callers could not state whether setup should install the daemon, so downstream clients had to rely on an implicit CLI default.

In the Windows Companion beta.2 path this surfaced as a lost Gateway connection during `run-wizard`, before the Companion could finish its own lifecycle and verification steps.

Downstream consumer: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#999.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns the RPC process and request boundary, so both fixes belong in the same owner seam:

- run setup and channel RPC wizards with `createNonExitingRuntime()`;
- treat only `ExitError(0)` as normal wizard completion;
- preserve non-zero exits as explicit session errors;
- add optional `installDaemon` to `WizardStartParamsSchema` and forward `true`, `false`, or omission unchanged;
- keep RPC safety defaults `skipUi: true` and `suppressGatewayTokenOutput: true` explicit.

This consolidates and replaces #109412 so the protocol contract and host-lifecycle fix are reviewed together rather than as overlapping edits to the same handler and tests.

## User Impact

Remote onboarding and channel setup no longer own the lifecycle of the Gateway hosting their session. Clients can explicitly opt into or out of daemon installation, while omitted input preserves existing setup defaults. Invalid/failing wizard exits remain visible as errors.

## Evidence

Exact proof head: `76ea9be30531d7eae9fff4e8c2f7402460e3cdca`.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound android-release-signing exec operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded `execFileSync` calls in `android-release-signing.mjs` (`run()` and `runText()` helpers) that could hang indefinitely when the executed command (e.g., `jarsigner`, `zipalign`, `openssl`) is unresponsive.

## Why This Change Was Made

All `execFileSync` calls to external commands must include a timeout and kill signal. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109325 (docker attestation) and #110464 (verify-stable-main-closeout).

## User Impact

Android release signing steps will fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely on hung tooling processes.

## Evidence

- Adds `ANDROID_SIGNING_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to both `run()` and `runText()` helpers.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/android-release-signing.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches `scripts/verify-docker-attestations.mjs` (#109325).

AI-assisted: built with Codex

---

### Real behavior proof

Probe on PR head: extracted the `run()` helper, shimmed the target command to block forever, and verified the bounded call exits with a timeout error instead of hanging.

```text
$ node proof-android-signing-timeout.mjs
entrypoint: run("sleep", ["infinity"])
fixture: command blocks forever
timeout: ANDROID_SIGNING_TIMEOUT_MS=500ms (scaled down for proof)
status: 1
stderr: Command failed: sleep infinity
        (timed out after 500ms)
```

The production deadline is 120 s; the proof scales it to 500 ms to keep the test fast. The `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the process is terminated, not just detached. Both `run()` and `runText()` helpers use the same constant and pattern.

target.title: fix(ui): Skills page shows Unavailable security badges because verdicts never hydrate on first load
target.body:
Closes #108647

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI Skills page showed a yellow **Unavailable** security badge for linked ClawHub skills on first load, even when the gateway's `skills.securityVerdicts` already reported `ok=true / decision=pass / securityStatus=clean`. The badge implied a broken or unverified skill when only the UI's verdict cache was empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

The route loader hydrates the `skills.status` report but never fetches security verdicts, and `ensureInitialData()` short-circuits once route data is present — so the only code path that populates `clawhubVerdicts` (`loadSkills` → `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts`) never ran on first paint. Additionally nothing retried: if the verdict loader ran while `connected` was transiently false it cleared the map silently.

The fix exports the existing `loadClawHubSecurityVerdicts` helper and (1) calls it from `applyRouteData()` whenever the route provides a report, reusing the exact production loader (no-linked-skills fast path, agent-scope guards, error handling included), and (2) backfills from `ensureInitialData()` — invoked on every gateway state change — whenever a report is loaded but the verdict map is empty; the helper's early return keeps this RPC-free when no linked ClawHub skills exist.

The branch is rebuilt on current `main` after the Web Awesome Control UI refactor (#106865): the earlier revision of this PR also fixed `applyRouteData()` copying a stale loader-time `connected:false` over the live connection state, which is exactly the "client present while `connected === false`" observation in the issue; `main` now reads `connected` from the live gateway snapshot itself, so that part of the fix is already absorbed and no longer in this diff.

Follow-up from review: while the verdict fetch is actually in flight, linked-skill badges now render the existing **Pending** state (neutral styling) instead of **Unavailable**, so an in-progress verification is never presented as a failed or unavailable security state. Only a settled empty verdict map reads as Unavailable. No new i18n keys (reuses `skillsPage.verdict.pending`).

## User Impact

Skills page security badges are correct on first load: clean linked ClawHub skills show **Clean** instead of a false **Unavailable**, including when route data races the gateway connection. No extra RPC when no linked ClawHub skills exist.

## Evidence

**Real Control UI runs** (real gateway `openclaw gateway run --dev` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, real ClawHub skill installed via `openclaw skills install karpathy-coding-guidelines`, backend verdict confirmed via `openclaw gateway call skills.securityVerdicts` → `decision:"pass"`, `securityStatus:"clean"`; macOS, Node 24.18):

- **Before:** navigating to `/skills` rendered the skill card with badge **Unavailable**; live page state showed `verdictKeys=[]`, `verdictsError=null` while the gateway verdict was clean — hydration was simply never triggered.
- **After (current head, on the post-refactor page):** the same navigation renders **Ready / Clean** for the linked skill; live page state: `connected=true`, `verdictKeys=["https://clawhub.ai / karpathy-coding-guidelines / 1.0.0"]`, `verdictsError=null`, `reportSkills=58`.

**Automated coverage** — the route-data page test fails without the `applyRouteData()` hydration call (verified by temporarily disabling it) and passes with it:

```
pnpm test ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.test.ts ui/src/lib/skills/index.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  41 passed (41)

pnpm tsgo:test:ui   # clean
pnpm ui:build       # clean
```

- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.test.ts` (new): a route-provided report hydrates verdicts; `ensureInitialData()` backfills an empty verdict map when a report is already loaded.
- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.test.ts`: a linked skill renders **Pending** (and not Unavailable) while `clawhubVerdictsLoading` is true, and still renders **Unavailable** for a settled empty verdict map. Full UI suite green: 306 files / 4363 tests.
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.test.ts`: the exported helper issues one `skills.securityVerdicts` request for linked reports and stays RPC-free for reports without linked skills.

**On the red `checks-node-compact-small-2` shard:** the failure is a single `src/tui/tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts` timeout ("timed out waiting for PTY exit") — a TUI PTY e2e path this UI-only diff does not touch. The same file passes locally on this branch with a fresh build and clean test state: 10/10 tests green.

Note: contributor checkout without Crabbox/Testbox access; the Control UI runs above are real local gateway + browser sessions on this branch.

target.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running browser screenshot with a configured image-understanding model would have the session become unusable when that vision model failed: later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` tool results were framed as image analysis until `/new`.

The vision-failure path previously fell back to injecting a raw base64 image block into the tool result. That image-bearing result is retained across recent completed turns, so it keeps re-entering model context and contaminates subsequent tool use.

This is the failure path described in #106703 (and the same root cause reported in #105305).

## Why This Change Was Made

The vision success path already returns a text-only description. This change makes the configured-vision failure path consistent with it: on describe failure, return a text-only result that reports the failure reason and keeps the staged outbound-copy path so the screenshot can still be shared explicitly via the message tool. Never write base64 image data into session/tool-result state on that path.

Scoped intentionally:

- Configured vision model throws: text-only (fixed path). A user who configured image understanding opted into text descriptions, so a transient provider error should not silently switch to dumping raw base64.
- Image understanding skipped / not configured (`describeBrowserScreenshot` returns `null`): still returns the raw image, so vision-capable primary models that rely on seeing the screenshot are unaffected.

## User Impact

When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the session stays usable: tool results remain text-framed, and the screenshot can still be shared via the message tool. Users without image understanding configured keep the previous model-visible screenshot behavior.

## Evidence

### Live createBrowserTool handler + browser control service (primary proof)

This is the proof ClawSweeper asked for: the changed `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot **catch** runs against a real managed Chrome tab through the in-process browser control service (not vitest mocks), configured vision fails through the real `describeImageFile` runtime, and a later `browser snapshot` in the same session stays text-only with zero image content blocks.

Reproduce (from this branch; needs local Chrome):

```
cd ~/oss-openclaw-106703   # or your checkout of fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback
git checkout fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback
pnpm install
pnpm exec tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts
```

Redacted live transcript (2026-07-18, head `e1fba23acb5`; no base64 bytes, no private paths):

```
=== Step 1: start browser (real browser control service) ===

=== Step 2: open proof page (real browser control service) ===
opened tab targetId: [redacted-tab-id]
proof page url: https://example.com/

=== Step 3: screenshot via real createBrowserTool().execute() (configured vision fails) ===
[media-understanding] image: failed (0/1) reason=Unknown model
--- real screenshot handler catch path ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: [browser screenshot vision failed: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini]
[Screenshot saved to "[redacted-path]/outbound/[redacted].png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.]
details.vision.failed: true
details.vision.error: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini

=== Step 4: later snapshot in same session (real handler) ===
--- real snapshot handler (later tool call) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: (wrapped external browser snapshot text; truncated)

result: PASS
```

To force a provider HTTP failure instead of model resolution (401/503 from a real endpoint), set a valid configured model ref plus an invalid key before running the script:

```
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-invalid-proof-key-replace-me
# ensure models.providers.openai.models includes your image model in the runtime config the script loads
pnpm exec tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts
```

### Real-handler behavioral proof (vitest; mocked vision throw only)

The reported symptom is a session-state effect: on a configured image-understanding failure the screenshot tool result previously carried a raw base64 image block, which is retained across recent completed turns (`pruneProcessedHistoryImages` keeps image blocks from the last `PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` completed turns) and forces later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` results into image-analysis framing until `/new`.

The proof drives the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot handler with the configured image-understanding call (`describeImageFile`) forced to fail, then drives a later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler. Only the vision call is mocked (to throw); the screenshot handler, its catch path, and the surrounding tool flow are real production code. It lives in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` under the describe block `browser screenshot vision-failure session-contamination proof (#106703, #105305)`.

Reproduce:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts -t "browser screenshot vision-failure session-contamination proof" --disableConsoleIntercept
```

Redacted transcript (content-block types and image-block counts only; no base64 bytes are printed):

```
--- real screenshot handler (configured vision failure) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: [browser screenshot vision failed: vision provider unavailable (HTTP 503)] \n [Screenshot saved to "/tmp/openclaw-media/outbound/share.png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.]
--- real snapshot handler (later tool call) ---
content-block types: [text]
image content blocks: 0
text: <<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT source="browser">>> \n ok \n <<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT>>>
=== session transcript (redacted) ===
user: screenshot the dashboard and summarize it
toolResult(browser:screenshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: the configured vision model was unavailable
user: now read the deploy status file
toolResult(read): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: deploy is green
user: take a page snapshot
toolResult(browser:snapshot): blocks=[text] images=0
assistant: captured snapshot
total image content blocks across session: 0
--- no-vision path (unchanged) screenshot result ---
content-block types: [text, image]
image content blocks: 1
text: browser:screenshot
```

Reading the transcript:

- Real screenshot handler with configured vision forced to fail: the emitted tool result is text-only (`image content blocks: 0`), carries the neutralized failure reason and the staged outbound-copy share hint, and sets `details.vision.failed` with no `details.media`.
- A later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler stays text-framed, and the reconstructed multi-turn session carries `total image content blocks: 0`, so nothing base64 rides alongside later `read` / `snapshot` results.
- No-vision path (unchanged): the same handler still reaches `imageResultFromFile` and emits a base64 image block (`image content blocks: 1`). This is the exact tool-result shape the pre-fix catch produced and that `pruneProcessedHistoryImages` preserves for recent turns, so the mechanism is real and the fix is scoped to the configured-vision-failure catch.

Honesty note: the vitest proof mocks only the single vision throw to isolate handler output shapes. The live handler script above uses real Chrome, the real browser control service, the real changed catch path, and the real `describeImageFile` runtime (no mock).

### Handler-side unit and regression tests

Focused tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` drive the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot path:

- `defangs vision failure fallback text and stays text-only`: vision-failure result is text-only (no `imageResultFromFile`, no image content block, no `details.media`) while preserving the neutralized failure text and share hint.
- `never injects a raw image block when configured vision fails (#106703, #105305)`: configured-vision failure returns zero image content blocks and marks `details.vision.failed`, so the result cannot persist an image across turns.
- No-vision (skipped/unconfigured) path still returns the raw image with sanitization.

### Local gate (redacted)

```
vitest extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts                          100 passed
vitest extensions/browser/src/browser/vision.test.ts                          6 passed
vitest src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.test.ts      12 passed
lint:extensions                                                             clean
format:check                                                                clean
tsgo:extensions:test                                                        0 errors
deadcode:full (knip production + all-exports)                               clean  (resolves check-dependencies unused-file)
live handler proof (scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-live-handler.ts)   PASS
```

Closes #106703
Related #105305

target.title: fix(scripts): bound release CI summary GitHub lookups
target.body:
## Problem

The full-release summary performs several synchronous GitHub CLI reads inside a five-minute verification job. Those reads and the manifest artifact download had no local deadline, so one stalled child could consume the job budget without identifying the failed operation.

## Solution

Route all release-summary GitHub operations through one release-owned runner with:

- a 60-second timeout;
- `SIGKILL` after the deadline;
- the existing plain-gh environment and 64 MiB read buffer;
- the artifact download's existing file-descriptor stdout destination.

The deadline matches the repository's npm release-recovery lookup budget. Required evidence reads still fail closed; the existing optional rate-limit telemetry keeps its local catch.

## Validation

- Focused Testbox run 29662977427: 43/43 release-summary tests passed.
- Full changed-surface Testbox gate passed: script declaration contracts, scripts/root-test TypeScript, formatting, and lint.
- Live helper proof on Testbox: a real `gh --version` process completed successfully; a deliberately stalled real child exited with `ETIMEDOUT` and `SIGKILL` through the production helper.
- Mandatory autoreview completed clean after the runner consolidation and again after the final type-safe assertion repair.
- Exact-head hosted CI run 29663188339 covers `e90f946459d8ed9f00e8502dbaf0fb80516d63e8`.

The original network-dependent 1 ms unit test was removed. Tests now inspect the production subprocess options deterministically, while live behavior proof remains outside the unit suite.

## Risk

A GitHub operation stalled for one minute now fails release verification and requires retry instead of occupying the surrounding job indefinitely. No authentication, endpoint, artifact-integrity, or release-evidence validation behavior changes.

Thanks to @tzy-17 for identifying the unbounded release lookup path and contributing the original fix.

target.title: fix(marketplaces): allow trusted feed key rotation
target.body:
## Summary

- compare newly verified signed feeds against persisted accepted monotonic metadata
- avoid requiring an old snapshot to verify under a newly rotated key merely to perform rollback comparison
- retain fail-closed fallback behavior when the old snapshot does not satisfy the current trust policy
- restore persisted monotonic metadata when signed snapshots are loaded from SQLite
- cover successful key rotation, lower-sequence rejection, and retained snapshot fallback through the durable store

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
A newly valid higher-sequence hosted feed could be rejected after trusted signing keys rotated because OpenClaw reverified the old snapshot with the new key before comparing sequences. The durable proof also exposed that SQLite stored accepted monotonic metadata but dropped it when reconstructing a snapshot.

Real environment tested:
Windows checkout using Node 24.15.0 and SQLite 3.51.3. The production hosted-catalog loader and real SQLite snapshot store were exercised with a temporary state database and generated Ed25519 Q2/Q3/Q4 key pairs. Network responses used the existing guarded-fetch harness so the signed bytes and trust transitions were deterministic.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\pnpm\store\v11\links\@\node\24.15.0\4b86559dec5f3e7def9c585f1a41d64f741f7930cf3b31f21bf2b4e73beef981\node_modules\node\bin\node.exe" scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run
```

The durable regression:
1. Opens the real SQLite marketplace state store.
2. Accepts sequence 8 signed by `acme-root-2026-q2`.
3. Reopens the persisted snapshot, replaces configured trust with `acme-root-2026-q3`, and accepts sequence 9.
4. Replaces configured trust with `acme-root-2026-q4` and rejects sequence 7.
5. Reloads the retained sequence 9 snapshot under the Q3 policy.

Evidence after fix:
The full catalog suite reported 46 tests passed. The key-rotation case persisted each accepted revision through SQLite and verified the retained snapshot after the rollback attempt.

Observed result after fix:
Sequence 9 was accepted under the rotated Q3 key. Sequence 7 under Q4 failed closed with the rollback diagnostic. Sequence 9 remained persisted and readable under its accepted Q3 policy. Persisted signed snapshots now reconstruct their accepted monotonic record from the authenticated body; unsigned rows cannot acquire that authority.

What was not tested:
A production publisher endpoint or production key-management system was not used. The proof intentionally uses generated keys and deterministic guarded network responses while exercising the real production loader and durable SQLite implementation.

## Validation

- full hosted catalog suite on Node 24.15.0 / SQLite 3.51.3: 46 passed
- targeted `oxfmt --check`
- targeted type-aware `oxlint`
- `git diff --check`
